{{Quote|The longer he stays away&hellip;the safer we'll all be!|Brador|<ref name="e14" />}}
'''Brador''' was an [[Ewok/Legends|Ewok]] member of the [[Bright Tree Village tribe]] on the [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon of Endor]]. In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], when the [[Youngling/Legends|young]] Ewok [[Teebo/Legends|Teebo]] was made [[Chief/Legends|leader]] for a [[Standard day/Legends|day]], Brador's [[Bordok/Legends|bordok]] was being uncooperative. Teebo tried to help, but he mistakenly made the bordok cause trouble all over the Ewok [[City/Legends|town]] of [[Bright Tree Village/Legends|Bright Tree Village]]. In anger, Brador organized a riot that tried to capture Teebo to prevent him from causing any more trouble, though Teebo eventually solved the problem for Brador himself by escaping on a [[Hang-glider/Legends|hang glider]].

==Biography==
===A squashy situation===
{{Quote|My ''squash melons!'' Look what you've done!|Brador|<ref name="e14" />}}
[[File:BradorMelons.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Brador chases after melons.]]
Brador was an [[Ewok/Legends|Ewok]] who lived among the [[Bright Tree Village tribe]] in the [[City/Legends|settlement]] of [[Bright Tree Village/Legends|Bright Tree Village]] on the [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon of Endor]].<ref name="e14" /> In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="Date">{{InsiderCite|23|Star Wars Publications Timeline|''Star Wars'' Publications Timeline}} dates the events of the [[Star Wars: Ewoks (1985)|''Ewoks'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic series]], which include the events of [[Ewoks (1985) 14|''Ewoks'' 14]], to three [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after the events of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], which corresponds to [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]] according to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.</ref> the [[Chief/Legends|leader]] of the village, Chief [[Chirpa/Legends|Chirpa]], went away for a [[Standard day/Legends|day]] to visit the [[Spirit Tree (Endor)|Spirit Tree]]. At random, he selected the [[Youngling/Legends|young]] [[Scout/Legends|scout]] [[Teebo/Legends|Teebo]] to act as the head of the village in his absence. That day, Brador's [[Bordok/Legends|bordok]] was not cooperating with the Ewok's efforts to get it to move a [[Wagon/Legends|wagon]] of [[squash melon]]s to a storage hut, with the bordok acting stubbornly and refusing to move. Teebo went up to Brador, inquiring about the latter's trouble.<ref name="e14" />

The young leader told Brador that the solution was simple&mdash;all Brador had to do was show the bordok who was in charge. Brador was confused by his answer, so Teebo gave a visual demonstration, whacking the bordok's rear end. However, the bordok reared back on its [[Limb/Legends|legs]] and began galloping away, causing the squash [[Fruit/Legends|melons]] to fall out of the wagon while Brador explained to Teebo that whacking the bordok was the one thing that could not be done to it. Brador ran after the wagon, angry at Teebo and warning the villagers that a runaway bordok was on the loose. Its wagon wound up destroying someone's [[Clothing/Legends|laundry]], a brand new hut, and pottery, eventually calming down and stopping. When Brador was asked who was responsible for all of the mayhem, the Ewok told them that Teebo had started it, asking that they seize him before he made anything worse.<ref name="e14" />

===A riot ensues===
{{Quote|<nowiki />''Teebo'' started it! Get him before things get worse!|Brador|<ref name="e14" />}}
[[File:Brador.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Brador argues with Kintaka and Warrick.]]
A small riot began, which ran after Teebo in the hopes of capturing him. Teebo tried to escape, asking his friends, [[Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka/Legends|Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka]] and [[Wicket Wystri Warrick/Legends|Wicket Warrick]], for help, but Kintaka first asked the rioters what they had against Teebo. One of them assured the [[Prince/Legends|princess]] that they meant no harm, with Brador adding that they only intended on [[Prisoner/Legends|imprisoning]] him to prevent him from destroying the village.<ref name="e14" />

Warrick asked that they all calm down in order to discuss the matter at hand in a civilized manner, but Brador then noticed and pointed out that Teebo was escaping on a [[Hang-glider/Legends|hang glider]]. Warrick shouted for him to come back, but two of the other Ewoks disagreed, glad to be rid of him and his chaos. Kintaka scolded the Ewoks for being unfair to Teebo, but Brador maintained the group's position, noting that they would all be safer the longer he was away from the village.<ref name="e14" />

Later that day, all of the Ewoks in the village were put under the influence of [[Necklace/Legends|necklaces]] that contained the [[stones of obedience]] and were forced to load [[Gemstone/Legends|gems]] for the [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Zornak]]. However, Teebo was able to save them all by using the stones against Zornak and freeing the Ewoks of the mind control, allowing them to return to the village. The general feeling toward Teebo shifted from disgust to celebration.<ref name="e14" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Don't let him get away!|Brador|<ref name="e14" />}}
Brador became very angry at Teebo when he caused the former's bordok to run all over the village causing trouble, going as far as recruiting the other Ewoks to lead a revolt against their temporary leader. Brador felt that the longer Teebo was gone, the safer the village would be, a sentiment that was shared by other villagers. Brador had [[Color/Legends|blue]] [[Hair/Legends|fur]] save for a mustache, which was orange, and eyebrows, which were black. Brador also had light skin and black [[Eye/Legends|eyes]].<ref name="e14" />

==Equipment==
Brador used a bordok and wagon to transport squash melons and wore a gray hood. The Ewok's clothing also utilized a cross strap and [[Belt/Legends|belt]].<ref name="e14" />

==Behind the scenes==
Brador appeared in the [[Ewoks (1985) 14|fourteenth issue]] of the [[Star Wars: Ewoks (1985)|''Ewoks'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic series]], which was written by [[David Manak]], illustrated by [[Warren Kremer]], and published by [[Marvel Comics]]<ref name="e14" /> on [[March 31]], [[1987]].<ref name="MarvelAge">{{BookCite|title=[[Marvel Age]]|number=Vol. 1 No. 51|publisher=[[Marvel Comics]] Group|date=[[June]] [[1987]]|issn=8750-4367}}</ref>
